chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb ibn Mītham who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) say: A fire will emerge from the depths of Aden, illuminating the necks of camels; it will be visible from the land of Shām, driving people towards the Gathering Place.

key_terms.أَعْنَاقُ الْإِبِلِ: the necks of camels (indicating great height/brightness)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the fire from Aden in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the physical reality of the Resurrection signs, specifically the 'Fire of Aden' which serves as a divine guide rather than merely a punishment. Its visibility from the Levant to Yemen underscores the universality of the call to the Mahshar, a concept deeply rooted in the eschatological narratives of the Ahl al-Bayt. This event is often interpreted as a manifestation of Allah's power to gather creation, reinforcing the certainty of the Hereafter.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 13.Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb ibn Mītham who said, “

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, ‘A fire will come out from inside the city of Aden by which the necks of camels[1] will be illuminated. It will be visible from the land of Shām and will drive people towards the [gathering] plain of maḥshar.’”
